chunks: Al-Ḥalabī asked him about the slaughtered animal of the Murji'ite and the Harūrī. He said:
So he said: "Eat, and be at ease and settled until whatever is to happen occurs."

key_terms.اسْتَقِرَّ: remain settled and stable without disturbance
key_terms.الْحَرُورِيِّ: a Harūrī; a Kharijite-associated sectarian designation mentioned in the question
key_terms.الْمُرْجِئِ: a Murji'ite; a member of the Murji'ah mentioned in the question
key_terms.حَتَّى: until; indicating continuance up to a future point
key_terms.ذَبِيحَةِ: the slaughtered animal or meat obtained through ritual slaughter
key_terms.قِرَّ: be at ease; remain calm and reassured

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the slaughtered animal of the Murji'ite and the Harūrī in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning eating the slaughtered animal of certain sectarian groups. The Imam عليه السلام replies with a brief directive permitting eating it and remaining at ease until future developments unfold.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4179 - Al-Halabi asked him about the slaughtered animal of the Murji'ite and the Haruri.
Imam (as) said: "Eat, and be at ease and settled until whatever is to happen occurs."
